title: The Mystery of the Purr
paras: For a long time, scientists believed that cats purred only when they were happy.
It is true that a relaxed cat often purrs while it is being petted or resting in a warm place.
However, researchers have noticed that cats also purr in very different situations.
Cats sometimes purr when they are injured, when they are giving birth, or even when they are close to death.
These observations suggest that purring is not simply a sign of pleasure.
One theory proposes that the low vibrations of a purr help bones and muscles heal.
Studies have shown that sounds at similar frequencies can make bones stronger in humans.
Another explanation focuses on communication.
Kittens begin to purr when they are only a few days old, which lets their mother know that they are safe and feeding well.
Adult cats may keep this behavior because it calms both themselves and the people around them.
Scientists still debate which explanation is correct, and it is possible that purring serves several purposes at once.

qs.stem: According to paragraph 1, what did scientists believe for a long time?
opts: Cats purred to communicate with people.
Purring showed that a cat was happy.
Only young cats were able to purr.
Purring helped cats stay warm.
qs.ex: Первое предложение: «scientists believed that cats purred only when they were happy». Верный вариант — перефраз этой мысли.

qs.stem: Select the sentence in paragraph 2 that gives evidence supporting the healing theory.
qs.ex: Теорию о заживлении вводит третье предложение, а доказательство даёт четвёртое: исследования показали, что звуки похожей частоты укрепляют кости у людей. Ищем именно evidence, а не саму теорию.

qs.stem: The word "proposes" in the passage is closest in meaning to
opts: proves
rejects
suggests
describes
qs.ex: Theory proposes — теория предполагает. Proves («доказывает») — ловушка: теория ещё не доказана, учёные спорят.

qs.stem: The word "their" in paragraph 3 refers to
opts: kittens
scientists
adult cats
people
qs.ex: «Kittens begin to purr …, which lets their mother know» — мать котят. Their относится к kittens.

qs.stem: What can be inferred about a cat that purrs while it is injured?
opts: It is probably feeling pleasure.
It may be purring for a reason other than happiness.
It is trying to call its kittens.
It will soon stop purring completely.
qs.ex: Абзац 2: такие наблюдения показывают, что мурлыканье — не просто знак удовольствия. Значит, раненая кошка мурлычет, скорее всего, по другой причине. Прямо это о конкретной кошке не сказано — это вывод.

title: The Paperback Revolution
paras: Until the 1930s, most new books in Britain were sold in hardcover.
They were well made but expensive, so many readers borrowed books from libraries instead of buying them.
Some publishers did print cheap paper editions, but these were usually poorly made and offered light entertainment rather than serious literature.
In 1935, a publisher named Allen Lane started a company called Penguin.
His idea was simple: he would print serious books with paper covers and sell them for the price of a pack of cigarettes.
Other publishers predicted that the plan would fail.
They believed that cheap books would lower the status of literature and reduce their own profits.
Instead, Penguin sold three million copies in its first year.
Penguin's success changed the book trade.
Paperbacks could be sold in railway stations, shops, and newsstands, not only in bookstores.
As a result, reading became a more common activity among working people, who could now afford to build small collections of their own.
Within a few years, other companies had copied the format, and the paperback became a normal part of everyday life.

insert.sentence: He is said to have had the idea at a railway station, where he could find nothing good to read for his journey.

qs.stem: According to paragraph 1, why did many readers borrow books from libraries?
opts: Libraries had more interesting books.
New books were expensive.
Hardcover books were badly made.
Bookstores were far from their homes.
qs.ex: «They were well made but expensive, so many readers borrowed books». Badly made — ловушка: в тексте наоборот, well made.

qs.stem: Why does the author mention "the price of a pack of cigarettes"?

hl.w: the price of a pack of cigarettes

opts: To show that Lane also sold cigarettes
To explain how cheap the books were meant to be
To criticize the habits of readers at that time
To compare the quality of books and cigarettes
qs.ex: Вопрос о функции фрагмента: автор сравнивает цену книги с ценой пачки сигарет, чтобы показать, насколько дёшево Лейн собирался продавать книги.

qs.stem: What can be inferred about other publishers in 1935?
opts: They did not expect so many people to buy cheap books.
They had already tried selling paperbacks.
They helped Lane start his company.
They lowered the price of hardcover books.
qs.ex: Они предсказывали провал, а Penguin продал три миллиона экземпляров за год. Значит, они недооценили спрос на дешёвые книги.

qs.stem: Look at the four squares [■] in paragraph 2 that indicate where the following sentence could be added. Where would the sentence best fit?
qs.ex: Вставляемое предложение рассказывает, откуда у Лейна появилась идея. Следующее предложение начинается с «His idea was simple» — оно продолжает тему идеи, поэтому вставка идёт сразу после основания компании, перед ним.

qs.stem: According to paragraph 3, all of the following are true of paperbacks EXCEPT:
opts: They were sold in railway stations.
They helped working people build collections.
They were sold only in bookstores.
They changed the book trade.
qs.ex: В тексте: «not only in bookstores» — не только в книжных. Вариант «only in bookstores» противоречит тексту.

title: Urban Heat Islands
paras: Cities are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them, a phenomenon known as the urban heat island effect.
Measurements in some large cities have recorded differences of more than ten degrees between downtown streets and nearby farmland.
The difference is usually greatest at night, when rural areas cool quickly but cities continue to release heat.
Several features of urban environments contribute to this warming.
Dark surfaces such as asphalt roads and rooftops absorb a large share of the sunlight that reaches them and store it as heat.
Tall buildings trap this heat and block the winds that might otherwise carry it away.
In addition, cars, air conditioners, and factories release heat directly into the air.
The consequences go beyond discomfort.
Higher temperatures increase the demand for air conditioning, which in turn raises energy consumption and, in many places, air pollution.
During heat waves, elderly residents and people without access to cooling face serious health risks.
To address the problem, some cities are painting roofs white, expanding parks, and planting trees along streets, since vegetation cools the air through the evaporation of water from leaves.

qs.stem: According to paragraph 1, when is the difference in temperature between cities and rural areas greatest?
opts: In the early morning
During heat waves
At night
In the middle of the day
qs.ex: «The difference is usually greatest at night» — ночью: село остывает быстро, а город продолжает отдавать тепло.

qs.stem: The word "trap" in the passage is closest in meaning to
opts: create
hold in
reflect
measure
qs.ex: Здания «trap this heat and block the winds that might otherwise carry it away» — удерживают тепло, не дают ему уйти. Trap = hold in.

qs.stem: Which of the sentences below best expresses the essential information in the highlighted sentence in paragraph 3? Incorrect choices change the meaning in important ways or leave out essential information.
opts: Because people use more air conditioning when it is hot, energy use rises and pollution often increases.
Air conditioning makes cities hotter, which is the main cause of pollution.
Energy consumption and air pollution are the main reasons why cities are hotter.
When pollution increases, people use air conditioning more often in hot weather.
qs.ex: Цепочка в оригинале: жара → больше кондиционеров → больше энергии → часто больше загрязнения. Вариант A сохраняет эту причинно-следственную цепочку. B и C переворачивают причину и следствие, D меняет порядок звеньев.

qs.stem: Why does the author mention "elderly residents" in paragraph 3?
opts: To give an example of people for whom heat can be dangerous
To explain why cities use more air conditioning
To show that older people prefer to live in cities
To argue that cities should build more hospitals
qs.ex: Абзац говорит о последствиях жары. Пожилые жители — пример тех, для кого жара — серьёзный риск для здоровья. Это функция примера, а не отдельный аргумент.

qs.stem: Select the sentence in paragraph 3 that explains how plants reduce temperatures.
qs.ex: Последнее предложение: растительность охлаждает воздух за счёт испарения воды с листьев (evaporation of water from leaves).

title: Why Prices End in 99
paras: Walk into almost any store and you will see prices such as $4.99 or $19.99 rather than $5 or $20.
This practice, known as charm pricing, is so common that many shoppers no longer notice it.
Yet economists and psychologists have found that it can have a measurable effect on what people buy.
The most widely accepted explanation involves the way people read numbers.
Because we read from left to right, the first digit makes the strongest impression.
A price of $2.99 therefore feels closer to $2 than to $3, even though the difference from $3 is only one cent.
In one experiment, a clothing company found that a dress sold more often at $39 than at $34, a price that was actually lower.
Charm pricing does not work in every situation, however.
Luxury brands often avoid it because they want customers to associate their products with quality rather than bargains.
For them, a round number such as $200 sends a message of confidence and simplicity.
Retailers must therefore decide whether they want a price to look cheap or to look prestigious.

qs.stem: The word "it" in paragraph 1 refers to
opts: a store
charm pricing
a price of $5
a shopper
qs.ex: «This practice, known as charm pricing, is so common that many shoppers no longer notice it» — покупатели не замечают саму практику, то есть charm pricing.

qs.stem: According to paragraph 2, why does $2.99 seem closer to $2 than to $3?
opts: Shoppers usually round prices down.
The first digit has the strongest effect on the reader.
Stores display the cents in small print.
People cannot calculate small differences.
qs.ex: Мы читаем слева направо, и первая цифра производит самое сильное впечатление (the first digit makes the strongest impression).

qs.stem: Why does the author mention the dress that sold more often at $39 than at $34?
opts: To show that a price ending in 9 can attract buyers even when it is higher
To explain why clothing is more expensive than other goods
To argue that companies should raise their prices
To show that shoppers always choose the lowest price
qs.ex: Пример с платьем доказывает силу «девятки»: цена $39 продавала лучше, чем более низкая $34. D прямо противоречит примеру.

qs.stem: According to paragraph 3, which of the following is NOT given as a reason luxury brands avoid charm pricing?
opts: They want their products to be linked with quality.
Round numbers suggest confidence.
Round numbers are easier for cashiers to process.
They do not want to look like bargains.
qs.ex: Про удобство для кассиров в тексте ничего нет. Остальные три причины названы в абзаце 3.

qs.stem: What can be inferred about a shop that prices a watch at $500 instead of $499?
opts: It probably wants the watch to seem high-quality.
It made a mistake when setting the price.
It expects to sell more watches than its competitors.
It is trying to attract customers looking for bargains.
qs.ex: Круглая цена, по тексту, — сигнал качества и уверенности, так делают люксовые бренды. Значит, магазин, скорее всего, хочет, чтобы часы выглядели престижно.

title: How Migrating Birds Find Their Way
paras: Each autumn, millions of migratory birds travel thousands of kilometers to wintering grounds they may never have seen before, often flying at night and over open ocean.
How they find their way has puzzled biologists for more than a century.
Experiments have shown that birds draw on several sources of information.
Some species orient themselves by the position of the sun, compensating for its movement across the sky with an internal clock.
Others learn the patterns of stars that rotate around the North Star, a skill that young birds appear to acquire by watching the night sky before their first migration.
Yet birds kept in windowless rooms still attempt to fly in the correct seasonal direction, which suggests that celestial cues cannot be the whole story.
The most intriguing candidate is the Earth's magnetic field.
When researchers placed robins in cages surrounded by artificial magnetic fields, the birds shifted their preferred direction to match the altered field.

Remarkably, this sense appears to depend on light: the response disappeared under certain wavelengths, leading scientists to propose that birds may literally see magnetic fields through specialized molecules in their eyes.
If confirmed, this mechanism would represent one of the most unusual sensory systems known in nature.

qs.stem: Which of the sentences below best expresses the essential information in the highlighted sentence in paragraph 2? Incorrect choices change the meaning in important ways or leave out essential information.
opts: Birds that cannot see the sky usually fly in the wrong direction during migration.
Celestial cues are the main reason why birds fly in the correct direction each season.
Since birds in rooms without windows still choose the right direction, they must use something besides the sun and stars.
Scientists kept birds in windowless rooms to prevent them from seeing the stars.
qs.ex: Суть: птицы без доступа к небу всё равно выбирают верное направление → значит, солнце и звёзды — не единственный ориентир. A противоречит оригиналу, B переворачивает вывод, D пересказывает деталь и теряет главное.

qs.stem: The word "intriguing" in the passage is closest in meaning to
opts: fascinating
confusing
reliable
obvious
qs.ex: Intriguing — интригующий, очень интересный. Confusing — ловушка по созвучию смысла «загадочный», но слово описывает интерес, а не путаницу.

qs.stem: What can be inferred about young birds before their first migration?
opts: They already know the position of the North Star from birth.
They need to observe the night sky to learn how to use the stars.
They cannot travel at night.
They follow older birds instead of the stars.
qs.ex: Навык ориентироваться по звёздам молодые птицы, судя по всему, приобретают, наблюдая ночное небо до первой миграции. Значит, это умение не врождённое и требует наблюдения.

qs.stem: According to paragraph 3, what happened when robins were placed in artificial magnetic fields?
opts: They stopped trying to migrate.
They changed the direction they preferred.
They became unable to see light.
They flew toward the North Star.
qs.ex: «The birds shifted their preferred direction to match the altered field» — сменили предпочтительное направление вслед за изменённым полем.

qs.stem: Why does the author mention that the response "disappeared under certain wavelengths"?
opts: To show that robins dislike some colors of light
To support the idea that the magnetic sense depends on light
To explain why birds migrate at night
To suggest that the experiment was poorly designed
qs.ex: Факт с длинами волн — доказательство тезиса «this sense appears to depend on light». Вопрос о функции: деталь подкрепляет мысль о связи магнитного чувства со светом.

title: From Tokens to Tablets
paras: Writing is often described as a sudden invention, but in Mesopotamia it seems to have developed gradually from practical needs.
Long before the first written texts, farmers and traders used small clay tokens of different shapes to keep track of goods such as grain and livestock.
Around 3500 BCE, officials began sealing these tokens inside hollow clay containers to guarantee that a shipment had not been altered.
Because a sealed container could not be checked without breaking it, they pressed the tokens into its surface before closing it, leaving visible marks.
Eventually, administrators realized that the marks alone were sufficient.
The tokens themselves could be abandoned, and signs drawn on flat clay tablets took their place.
Over the following centuries, this system of accounting expanded.
Scribes added signs for numbers and for the names of people, and later used symbols to represent sounds as well as objects.
Only at this point could writing record language in general, including stories, laws, and letters.
The earliest writing, in other words, was not designed to preserve literature but to manage an economy.

insert.sentence: In other words, the outside of the container now recorded exactly what was inside.

qs.stem: According to paragraph 1, what were clay tokens used for?
opts: Decorating containers
Recording quantities of goods
Writing down stories
Paying taxes to officials
qs.ex: Жетоны использовали «to keep track of goods such as grain and livestock» — вести учёт товаров.

qs.stem: The word "they" in paragraph 2 refers to
opts: tokens
containers
officials
shipments
qs.ex: Кто вдавливал жетоны в поверхность сосуда? Люди — officials из предыдущего предложения. Tokens — ловушка: это ближайшее существительное во мн. ч., но жетоны сами себя не вдавливают.

qs.stem: Look at the four squares [■] in paragraph 2 that indicate where the following sentence could be added. Where would the sentence best fit?
qs.ex: «In other words» пересказывает предыдущую мысль: на поверхности сосуда остались отпечатки жетонов — значит, снаружи было видно, что внутри. Поэтому вставка идёт сразу после предложения про отпечатки (visible marks).

qs.stem: According to paragraph 3, all of the following were added to the system EXCEPT:
opts: signs for numbers
names of people
symbols for sounds
maps of trade routes
qs.ex: Числа, имена и знаки для звуков названы в абзаце 3. Карт торговых путей в тексте нет.

qs.stem: How is the passage organized?
opts: It compares two competing theories about the origin of writing.
It traces how writing gradually developed from an earlier practice.
It describes a problem and explains why the solution failed.
It argues that writing was invented suddenly by one culture.
qs.ex: Текст идёт по этапам: жетоны → запечатанные сосуды с отпечатками → таблички → знаки для звуков. Это последовательное развитие. D противоречит первому предложению.
